sections.content: How many people are "engineering project managers and project engineers"?

31,005 people

were counted on the census as "engineering project managers and project engineers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Engineering project managers and project engineers schedule, manage and oversee engineering projects for quality of work, timeliness and completion within budge. They also plan, design and specify materials and equipment for the project and create necessary technical drawings.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "engineering project managers and project engineers" there were more men than women (83.8% compared with 16.2%).

This means "engineering project managers and project engineers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 83.8% and women made up 16.2% of "engineering project managers and project engineers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "engineering project managers and project engineers" included:

  • plastics process operatives
  • waste disposal and environmental services managers
  • assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "engineering project managers and project engineers", 15.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "engineering project managers and project engineers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "engineering project managers and project engineers" included:

  • quality control and planning engineers
  • other health professionals
  • other registered nursing professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "engineering project managers and project engineers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "engineering project managers and project engineers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "engineering project managers and project engineers", 5.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (95.1% compared with 4.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95%) than self-employed (5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
